lines: A polyphonic build of Mutable Instruments' Plaits: sixteen engines, up to sixteen voices, a unison spread and a tuning knob the hardware does not have
Steps forward through the eight tonal engines one press at a time, and brings the module back into that bank from a percussive engine
Steps forward through the eight percussive engines one press at a time, and moves the module into that bank from a tonal engine
Sets the octave, snapping to whole octaves unless Octave knob free tune is switched on; the panel numbers its positions 0 to 8 while the tooltip reads -4 to 4
Shifts the pitch by up to seven semitones either way, on top of the octave knob
The Plaits harmonics control; what it does depends on the engine, and the panel relabels it for whichever engine is chosen
The Plaits timbre control; what it does depends on the engine, and the panel relabels it for whichever engine is chosen
The Plaits morph control; what it does depends on the engine, and the panel relabels it for whichever engine is chosen
Crossfades the mixed output between the two other outputs, fully anticlockwise the first of them and fully clockwise the second
Sets the colour of the low pass gate: anticlockwise it closes the tone down as well as the level, clockwise it acts more as a plain amplifier with a longer tail
Sets the length of the internal envelope and of the low pass gate's decay
Sets how many voices run in unison, 1 to 16; left at 1 the voice count follows the number of channels patched to the pitch input instead
Spreads the unison voices apart in pitch: out to half a semitone over the first half of its travel, out to an octave by nine tenths, and then towards whole octaves apart
Scales how far the timbre input moves the timbre control, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the FM input moves the pitch, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre; it is ignored while the FM jack is empty
Scales how far the morph input moves the morph control, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the harmonics input moves the harmonics control, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the output mix input moves the mix, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the decay input moves the decay knob, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the colour input moves the colour knob, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the engine input moves the engine choice, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Scales how far the spread input moves the spread knob, and turns it upside down anticlockwise of the centre
Sets how far the internal envelope moves the timbre control, either way from nothing at the centre
Sets how far the internal envelope moves the pitch, either way from nothing at the centre; with the speech engine and a word bank chosen it sets the speech intonation instead
Sets how far the internal envelope moves the morph control, either way from nothing at the centre; with the speech engine and a word bank chosen it sets the speech speed instead
Sets how far the internal envelope moves the harmonics control, either way from nothing at the centre
Sets how far the internal envelope moves the output mix, either way from nothing at the centre
Chooses one of eight settings for what the second output carries while the wavetable engine runs, the same setting the menu offers
Moves the engine choice, 5V stepping across all sixteen engines before the knob above scales it
Moves the timbre control, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it
Frequency modulation, one volt shifting the pitch six semitones before the knob above scales it
Moves the morph control, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it
Moves the harmonics control, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it
Fires the internal envelope on a rising edge above 0.9V, reading low again below 0.3V, and a cable here is what switches that envelope on at all
Sets the level, 8V for full; a cable here takes the level away from the internal envelope and gives it to this jack
Sets the pitch at one volt per octave, and the number of channels patched here sets how many voices run
Moves the colour knob, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it, and the total is held between the knob's two ends
Moves the decay knob, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it, and the total is held between the knob's two ends
Moves the spread knob, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it; only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read here
Moves the output mix, 10V covering the whole of it before the knob above scales it
The engine's main output, one channel per voice; the panel names what it carries for whichever engine is chosen
The engine's second output, one channel per voice; the panel names what it carries for whichever engine is chosen
The other two outputs crossfaded by the mix knob, one channel per voice
Note — the lettering on the three large upper knobs and on two of the outputs changes with the engine, because the panel picture is swapped for a different one per engine
Note — the engine attenuverter and the wavetable output mode share one place on the panel: the mode knob appears there only while the wavetable engine is chosen and the engine input is empty
Note — the low pass gate is out of the circuit until either the trigger input or the level input has a cable in it, so the colour and decay knobs change nothing before that
Menu — Octave knob free tune — lets the octave knob move continuously instead of snapping to whole octaves
Menu — LFO Mode — drops every engine about nine octaves, into the range where they are useful as modulation sources
Menu — Show modulation amounts on knobs — draws a mark on each large knob showing where modulation has moved that control for each voice
Menu — Aux output mode for Wave Table engine — eight settings for what the second output carries while the wavetable engine runs, from a five bit version of the main output to a sine mixed into it
Menu — LPG mode: Classic (Low pass and VCA), Low pass, Bypassed — chooses whether the gate both filters and attenuates, only filters, or is taken out altogether
Menu — Resampling quality — sets the quality of the conversion from the engine's own 48000Hz to the rack's rate, and it only appears while the rack is not running at 48000Hz
Menu — Models — the sixteen engines listed by name, the first eight tonal and the last eight percussive, picking one directly

0.normal: 0V, so the engine the buttons chose
0.why: Palette.cpp:475-478 divides getVoltage(i) by 5 and multiplies by the attenuverter; voice.cc:113-118 feeds that to the engine quantizer over sixteen steps

1.why: Palette.cpp:491-494 divides getVoltage(i) by 10; voice.cc adds it to the timbre knob scaled by the attenuverter and constrains the sum to 0 and 1

2.normal: 0V, and the attenuverter is forced to zero
2.why: Palette.cpp:483-486 multiplies getVoltage(i) by 6; Palette.cpp:465-466 sets frequency_cv_amount to 0 unless this jack isConnected

3.why: Palette.cpp:495-498 divides getVoltage(i) by 10 before it is added to the morph knob

4.why: Palette.cpp:487-490 divides getVoltage(i) by 10; voice.cc:158 adds it to the harmonics knob and constrains the sum to 0 and 1

5.normal: no reading, and no internal envelope
5.why: Palette.cpp:500-509 divides getVoltage by 3; voice.cc:96 and :105 take it high above 0.3 and low below 0.1, which is 0.9V and 0.3V at the jack

6.why: Palette.cpp:511-520 divides getVoltage by 8; voice.cc:144-148 compresses it and clamps the result at zero, and uses 0.8 when the jack is unpatched

7.why: Palette.cpp:385 takes the voice count from getChannels; Palette.cpp:479-482 multiplies getVoltage(i) by 12 to give semitones

8.why: Palette.cpp:454-457 divides getVoltage(i) by 10, multiplies by the attenuverter, adds the knob and clamps the sum to 0 and 1

9.why: Palette.cpp:459-462 divides getVoltage(i) by 10, multiplies by the attenuverter, adds the knob and clamps the sum to 0 and 1

10.why: Palette.cpp:378-383 reads getVoltage with no channel argument, rescales the product with the attenuverter from -5 to 5 into -0.5 to 0.5 and clamps the sum to 0 and 1

11.why: Palette.cpp:569-575 uses getVoltage(i) when getChannels is above 1 and getVoltage(0) otherwise, rescaling from -5 to 5 into -0.5 to 0.5

0.why: Palette.cpp:560 calls setChannels with the voice count; :583 writes the engine output times -5

1.why: Palette.cpp:561 calls setChannels with the voice count; :584 writes the aux output times -5

2.why: Palette.cpp:562 calls setChannels with the voice count; :586 writes the crossfade of the other two

AtelierPalette.notes: A fourth output, PITCH_SPREAD_OUTPUT, is declared at Palette.cpp:92 but the widget never adds a jack for it and process() never writes it, so it has no line and no tag. Two parameters share the panel position at 18,76: the engine attenuverter and the wavetable output mode knob, swapped by the widget's step() at Palette.cpp:800-803 according to whether the wavetable engine is running with the engine input unpatched. Both are tagged, because a hidden widget is skipped when a click is resolved and only the visible one can ever be reached. The source comment at Palette.cpp:499 says the trigger input fires at around 0.7V; the code divides by 3 at :502 and plaits fires above 0.3 at voice.cc:96, which is 0.9V at the jack. The octave knob is configured -4 to 4 at Palette.cpp:147 while the panel numbers its positions 0 to 8. The panel is a stack of sixteen SVGs, one per engine, drawn over a common background at Palette.cpp:831-836, so the lettering on the harmonics, timbre and morph knobs and on the two single outputs changes with the engine. configInput is called twice for the engine input, at Palette.cpp:213 with "Engine choice CV" and again at :223 with "Engine CV"; the second wins, and the census carries the second. The low pass gate is bypassed at voice.cc:221-222 unless the level or trigger input is patched. addParam is called twice for the output mix knob at Palette.cpp:858-859, putting two widgets at the same place for the same parameter, which is harmless.
